AK.reason: AS 08.40.005-08.40.200 directly licenses and regulates electrical administrators (the Alaska term for electricians/electrical contractors), covering licensing requirements, examinations, fees, disciplinary actions, and enforcement.

AL.reason: The corpus is the Alabama Electrical Contractors Act (Chapter 34-36) which directly licenses electrical contractors, master electricians, and journeyman electricians in Alabama.

AR.reason: The corpus is Arkansas Code Title 17 Chapter 28 which directly licenses master electricians, journeyman electricians, electrical contractors, and related classifications in Arkansas.

AZ.reason: The corpus contains Arizona's contractor licensing statute (A.R.S. Title 32, Chapter 10) which explicitly covers specialty electrical contracting classifications and licenses electricians and electrical contractors under the registrar of contractors framework.

CA.reason: The corpus is California Business and Professions Code Chapter 9 (Contractors State License Law), which licenses and regulates contractors including electrical contractors under the C-10 specialty classification governed by this chapter.

CO.reason: Article 115 (sections 12-115-101 through 12-115-124) is the Colorado electricians licensing law, covering the state electrical board, licensing requirements for master electricians, journeyman electricians, residential wiremen, electrical contractors, and apprentices.

CT.reason: The corpus contains Connecticut Chapter 393 (Sec. 20-330 through 20-341) which explicitly defines electrical work, establishes the Electrical Work Board, and sets licensure requirements for electrical contractors and journeymen electricians.

DE.reason: The corpus contains Delaware's Board of Electrical Examiners chapter (§§ 1401-1425) which directly licenses master electricians, journeyperson electricians, limited electricians, apprentice electricians, and electrical contractors.

FL.reason: The corpus contains Florida Chapter 489 Part II (sections 489.501-489.558) which is the Electrical Contractors Licensing Law, along with Part I covering general construction contracting, both of which are present in the citation list.

GA.reason: The corpus is Georgia Code Chapter 43-14 which directly licenses and regulates electrical contractors, plumbers, conditioned air contractors, low-voltage contractors, and utility contractors, including specific provisions for electrical contractor licensing requirements.

HI.reason: Chapter 448E directly licenses and regulates electricians (journey worker, supervising, specialty, industrial, maintenance) in Hawaii, including examination, minimum requirements, fees, and enforcement provisions.

IA.reason: Iowa Code Chapter 103 directly licenses and regulates electricians and electrical contractors, including class A/B master electricians, journeyman electricians, apprentice electricians, and electrical contractors.

ID.reason: The corpus contains Idaho Code Title 54 Chapter 10, which directly licenses and regulates electrical contractors, journeyman electricians, master electricians, residential electricians, and related classifications in Idaho.

KY.reason: The citation list includes KRS 227A.010 through 227A.150, which is Kentucky's electrician licensing statute, and the chapter title explicitly covers electricians.

LA.reason: The corpus contains Louisiana RS 37:2150 et seq., the State Licensing Board for Contractors chapter, which explicitly includes Electrical as a major license classification and governs licensing of electrical contractors.

MA.reason: The corpus is Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 141 which directly licenses and regulates master electricians, journeyman electricians, systems contractors, and systems technicians, including examination, licensure, and enforcement provisions.

MD.reason: The corpus is Maryland GBO Title 6, which establishes the State Board of Electricians and directly licenses master electricians, journeyperson electricians, and apprentice electricians.

ME.reason: The corpus contains Maine's electrician licensing statutes (32 M.R.S. §§1101-1207) including definitions of master/journeyman/apprentice electricians, license requirements, the Electricians' Examining Board, examinations, renewals, and reciprocity.

MI.reason: The corpus is Michigan's Skilled Trades Regulation Act (Act 407 of 2016, MCL 339.5101 et seq.), which explicitly covers electrical contractors and electricians as a regulated skilled trade, including references to the Michigan electrical code and the former electrical administrative board.

MN.reason: Chapter 326B contains Minnesota's electrical licensing statutes including sections 326B.31-326B.399 and 326B.43-326B.49 which cover the Board of Electricity and electrical contractor/electrician licensing requirements.

MT.reason: MCA Title 37 Chapter 68 directly licenses and regulates electricians and electrical contractors in Montana, including master electricians, journeyman electricians, residential electricians, and electrical contractors.

NC.reason: The corpus contains NC General Statutes Article 87-39 through 87-51, which is the direct licensure law for electrical contractors in North Carolina, covering the licensing board, definitions, license classifications, fees, and enforcement.

ND.reason: Chapter 43-09 directly licenses and regulates master electricians, journeyman electricians, class B electricians, power limited electricians, and electrical contractors in North Dakota.

NH.reason: The corpus is NH RSA Chapter 319-C which directly licenses and regulates electricians including master electricians, journeyman electricians, and electrical contractors in New Hampshire.

NJ.reason: The corpus is the New Jersey Electrical Contractors Licensing Act (N.J.S.A. 45:5A-1 et seq.) which directly licenses electrical contractors, journeyman electricians, apprentice electricians, and wiremen.

NM.reason: The corpus is the New Mexico Construction Industries Licensing Act (Chapter 60, Article 13) which explicitly licenses electrical contractors, journeymen, and related electrical trades as part of its comprehensive construction licensing framework.

NV.reason: NRS Chapter 624 is Nevada's contractor licensing law covering the State Contractors Board, which licenses specialty contractors including electrical contractors, and the text explicitly references electrical specialty licensing requirements.

OH.reason: Chapter 4740 explicitly licenses electrical contractors through the Ohio Construction Industry Licensing Board, with sections covering application, examination, issuance, renewal, reciprocity, and discipline for electrical contractors.

OK.reason: The corpus contains the Oklahoma Electrical License Act (59-1680 through 59-1699) which directly licenses and regulates electrical contractors, journeyman electricians, and electrical apprentices.

OR.reason: ORS chapter 479 contains the Oregon Electrical Safety Law sections (479.510 through 479.995) which license and regulate electricians and electrical contractors, and those sections appear in the citation list.

RI.reason: The corpus is R.I. Gen. Laws Chapter 5-6, which directly licenses electrical contractors, journeyperson electricians, master electricians, and related trades in Rhode Island.

SC.reason: The corpus contains SC Chapter 40-11, the Contractors Licensing Board statute, which explicitly licenses mechanical contractors performing electrical work and includes board membership for electrical contractors, covering the licensure of electrical contractors in South Carolina.

SD.reason: The corpus is South Dakota chapter 36-16 which directly licenses electrical contractors, journeyman electricians, Class B electricians, and other electrician classifications, establishing the State Electrical Commission, examination and fee requirements, and related regulations.

TX.reason: The corpus is Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1305, the Texas Electrical Safety and Licensing Act, which directly licenses master electricians, journeyman electricians, electrical contractors, and related electrical occupations.

UT.reason: The corpus contains the Utah Construction Trades Licensing Act (Chapter 58-55) which explicitly licenses journeyman electricians, master electricians, apprentice electricians, general electrical contractors, residential electrical contractors, and related classifications.

VA.reason: The corpus contains Virginia Code Chapter 11 of Title 54.1 (Board for Contractors), which explicitly licenses electrical contractors as a classification under Class A, B, and C contractor licenses and requires a master tradesman license for electrical contractors.

VT.reason: The corpus contains Vermont's Electricians Licensing Board chapter (26 V.S.A. §§ 881-915) which directly licenses master electricians, journeyman electricians, and type-S journeyman electricians.

WA.reason: Chapter 19.28 RCW explicitly licenses electrical contractors, master electricians, and administrators, covering application requirements, examinations, bonds, inspections, and exemptions for the electrical contracting trade in Washington.
